name: Burnt areas mapped from space (EFFIS)
summary: Land that the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) mapped as burnt from satellite pictures near each city, in the last 30 days. Only larger fires are mapped.
tagline: EFFIS · every 6 h · no key · not yet verified

el.name: Καμένες εκτάσεις από το διάστημα (EFFIS)
el.summary: Γη που το Ευρωπαϊκό Σύστημα Πληροφοριών για τις Δασικές Πυρκαγιές (EFFIS) χαρτογράφησε ως καμένη από δορυφορικές εικόνες κοντά σε κάθε πόλη τις τελευταίες 30 ημέρες. Χαρτογραφούνται μόνο οι μεγαλύτερες πυρκαγιές.
el.tagline: EFFIS · κάθε 6 ώρες · χωρίς κλειδί · δεν έχει επαληθευτεί ακόμη

publisher.name: EFFIS, Copernicus Emergency Management Service (Joint Research Centre, European Commission)

licence.attribution: Burnt areas: EFFIS, Copernicus Emergency Management Service, © European Union, CC BY 4.0. Changed: dates and areas kept, summed by city

restrictions: Give appropriate credit and say that the data were changed (CC BY 4.0); the EFFIS pages give no exact credit line, the wording above is ours
EFFIS' data-license page ties reuse to the Commission Decision of 12 December 2011 on reuse of documents: a teacher reads it once before the layer goes active

coverage.area: Cyprus and nearby sea (box 31.3 to 34.9 E, 33.7 to 36.1 N)

update.note: EFFIS says burnt areas are updated daily; a fire is mapped a day or more after it, and only when it is large enough.

variables.note: Sum of the mapped burnt areas whose centre is within 50 km of the city centre and that were updated in the last 30 days. 0 when none.

quality.uncertainty: Outlines are mapped from satellite pictures, so edges are good to a few hundred metres. A fire is missing until it is mapped, and small fires may never be.
known_issues: Only larger fires are mapped: roughly 30 hectares or more (EFFIS says Sentinel-2 now also helps map smaller ones)
A map comes a day or more after the fire, so a fire that is burning now is usually not here yet: use the fire-hotspots layer for the last 24 hours
The sum covers outlines whose centre is within 50 km, so a very large fire can reach beyond it and a nearby one can be left out
0 means none mapped, not that nothing burnt
UNVERIFIED: the request, the layer name (nrt.ba.poly) and the property names come from a third-party client's README, not from an EFFIS page; never read live from our sandbox

upstream.name: EFFIS near-real-time burnt area perimeters, derived from MODIS, VIIRS and Sentinel-2 (the active fires EFFIS shows are NASA FIRMS data)

use_for: Saying how much land near a city was mapped as burnt in the last 30 days
not_for: Saying that a fire is burning now: a burnt-area map comes a day or more late
Saying that no fire happened because 0 is shown: small fires are not mapped

notes: Shipped as a planned layer on purpose: the WFS request is not documented on an EFFIS page, only in a third-party client. EFFIS' own hotspot layers are WMS images of NASA FIRMS data (no key, but no numbers either), so hotspots come from the fire-hotspots layer. After the first line 'EFFIS answered: N perimeters ...' shows in the production log, a teacher can set status to active. A WMS fallback was not built.

x_rules.window: perimeters whose last update (finaldate, else initialdate) is within 30 days before the list was fetched
x_rules.city: the area-weighted centre of the outer rings is within 50 km of the city centre
x_rules.area: the property 'area' (hectares) is used, only when the outline (outer rings, worked out here) is between 0.3 and 3 times that area; otherwise the feature is dropped as unreadable
x_rules.bad: a feature without a Polygon or MultiPolygon, a positive area, or a valid date is dropped; when none can be read, the layer reports an error, never 0
